title: Preface: A Guide for Introverts
titleTranslate: 前言：写给内向者的社交指南
text:
Hey, friend who stumbled upon this.

I think if you clicked on this, we might be quite similar.

We're the kind of people who, in crowded and lively situations, might be sitting there physically, but mentally we're already counting down, planning when we can make a "reasonable exit".

We have plenty of thoughts in our heads, but when words come to our lips, we always want to think them over a bit more, and in the end, we choose "Yeah, that's fine".

Rather than joining the crowd, we prefer to be alone doing something we like, or slowly chatting with one or two people we get along with.

These feelings, I know them all too well.

Don't think there's something wrong with you because of these things.

There really isn't.

This is just our way of interacting with the world, which is a bit different from some people.

But having said that, we do live among people, and work and life inevitably require cooperation and interaction with others.

I've also tried forcing myself to learn those particularly outgoing, naturally familiar behaviors, and it was exhausting.

I felt awkward, and others found it awkward too.

Later, I gradually understood: people like us don't need to twist ourselves into another kind of person at all.

What we need is a set of methods that are convenient and effortless, to handle those unavoidable moments when we need to interact with people.

This set of methods should be designed according to our own characteristics, such as thinking more, being more careful, and being able to understand others' feelings.

So, this guide came into being.

It doesn't preach empty inspiration, and it doesn't force you to become "social".

It just wants to do a few things: provide real situations you'll encounter, explain the principles clearly, chat like friends, let you be yourself, and cover various aspects of life.
textTranslate:
嘿，刷到这段话的朋友。

我想，你点开这个，咱俩可能挺像的。

就是那种，在人多热闹的场合，虽然人坐在那儿，但心里已经在默默倒计时，盘算着啥时候能"合理撤退"。

脑子里想法其实挺多，可话到嘴边，总想再琢磨琢磨，结果最后还是选择了"嗯，挺好"。

比起扎堆热闹，更愿意自己待着做点喜欢的事，或者跟一两个聊得来的人慢慢说说话。

这些感觉，我太知道了。

别为这些觉得是自己有问题。

真不是。

这只是咱们跟世界打交道的方式，跟有些人不太一样而已。

但话说回来，咱们毕竟生活在人堆里，工作、生活都免不了要跟人协作、来往。

我以前也试过，硬逼着自己去学那些特别外向、自来熟的样子，结果累得够呛，自己别扭，别人看着也别扭。

后来我才慢慢明白过来：咱们这样的人，压根不需要把自己拧巴成另一种人。

咱们需要的，是一套用着顺手、不费劲儿的方法，好应付那些躲不开的、需要跟人打交道的时刻。

这套方法，得是照着咱们自己的特点（比如想得多一点、细心一点、能体察别人感受）来设计的。

所以，才有了你看到的这份东西。

它不灌鸡汤，也不逼着你去变得"合群"。

它就想做这么几件事：全是你会遇到的真事儿，把道理掰碎了说，就像朋友间聊天，让你还是你，生活里的事儿多少都沾点。

title: Understanding Social Rules: It's Not About Becoming a Social Butterfly
titleTranslate: 理解社会运行的基本规则：不是让你变成"社牛"
text:
When we mention "understanding social etiquette", do you immediately think of those people who are eloquent at dinner parties and get along with everyone?

Do you feel that you can't learn that, and don't want to?

Don't worry, let's put that thought aside first.

The "understanding social etiquette" we're talking about isn't that mysterious.

It's more like installing new software on your phone.

It's not to make you change, but to make it more convenient to use, so you can handle daily small things without getting stuck or feeling awkward.

It's not about making you a "social butterfly", but about helping you "not get stuck".

We all live among people every day.

Picking up packages, ordering takeout, greeting colleagues at work, asking questions at service windows.

These all count.

The goal is never to make you the brightest star in the crowd.

It's to help you handle these unavoidable, daily small things more smoothly.

Don't make things complicated because you're nervous.

Many times we feel tired because we think of "interacting with people" as too "big", as if we have to perform perfectly every time.

Actually, there really isn't such a high requirement.

Often, being able to "say things clearly" and "not let the situation get too awkward" is already doing very well.

Our "social battery" is limited, and that's normal.

We have to admit that for many of us, interacting with people is quite draining.

It's not like charging, it's more like draining.

Quiet solitude is when we recharge.

This isn't shameful, it's just our "factory settings".

Trying hard to "drain" will only make you more tired, and even make you annoyed at seeing people.

So, stop struggling with "should I go" or "it's not good not to go".

This kind of struggle is the most draining.

Try giving a little "friendly signal".

Many small moments, like a smile, a nod, saying "thank you", are like "lubricants" in interpersonal relationships.

They don't require you to invest deep emotions.

They're more like sending a signal: "Hey, I'm here, no ill will."

Don't be afraid of having nothing to say.

Being a good "listener" is great.

Many people think that being social means being very talkative.

Actually, that's wrong!

In many situations, a patient listener who makes others feel comfortable is more popular than someone who talks non-stop.

"Being able to listen" and "understanding others" are precisely the strengths of many people like us.

Stop worrying about "not being able to respond".

The ultimate goal is to make "yourself comfortable", not to "make others like you".

You can't satisfy everyone, that's too tiring.

What we're learning is ultimately to feel more at ease in necessary social environments.

At the same time, protect that quiet place in your heart, and those few truly important relationships that don't drain you.

Don't completely negate yourself because of one wrong thing you said, or a few seconds of awkward silence.
textTranslate:
一提到"要懂点人情世故"，你是不是马上想到那些在饭局上能说会道、跟谁都混得熟的人？

觉得那套自己学不来，也不想学。

别急，咱先把这个想法放一放。

咱们要聊的"懂点人情世故"，其实没那么玄乎。

它更像给手机装个新软件，不是为了让你变个样，而是让你能用起来更顺手，处理些日常小事时不那么卡壳、不觉得别扭。

它不是让你变成"社牛"，而是让你"不卡壳"。

咱们每天都生活在人堆里，取快递、点外卖、上班跟同事打个招呼、去办事窗口问个事。

这些都算。

它的目的，从来不是让你去当人群里最亮眼的那颗星，而是帮你把这些躲不开的、天天要碰到的小事儿，处理得顺当点儿，别因为心里发怵反而把事儿搞复杂了。

很多时候咱们觉得累，是因为把"跟人打交道"想得太"大"了，好像每次都得表现完美。

其实真没那么高要求，很多时候，能"把事说清楚"、"别让场面太僵"，就已经做得很好了。

咱们的"社交电量"是有限的，这很正常。

得承认，对咱们很多人来说，跟人打交道是挺费神的，不像充电，更像耗电。

安静独处才是回血的时候。

这一点不丢人，就是咱们的"出厂设置"而已。

硬撑着去"耗电"，回来只会更累，甚至看见人都烦。

所以，别再纠结"我该去"还是"不去不好"了，这种纠结最耗神。

试着给出一点"友好的小信号"。

很多小瞬间，比如一个微笑、点个头、说句"谢谢"，其实就像人际间的"润滑剂"。

它们不需要你投入多深感情，更像是在传递一个信号："嗨，我在这儿，没恶意。"

别怕没话说，当好"听众"就很棒。

好多人以为会社交就得特别能说。

其实不对！

在很多场合，一个能耐心听别人说话、让人感觉舒服的听众，比一个不停说话的人更受欢迎。

而"听得进去"、"能理解别人"，恰恰是很多咱们这种人的长处。

别再为"接不上话"着急了。

最终是为了"自己舒服"，不是"让人喜欢"。

你不可能让所有人都满意，那样太累了。

咱们学这些，最终是想在必要的社交环境里待得自在一点，同时保护好自己心里那块安静的地方，还有那几个真正重要的、相处不累的关系。

别因为一次没说对话，或者冷场了几秒钟，就全盘否定自己。

title: Overcoming Social Anxiety: Breaking the Illusion
titleTranslate: 从根源上克服社交恐惧：打破错觉
text:
The "social anxiety" we talk about is often actually our brains "scaring ourselves".

You think it's because you're "tongue-tied" or "slow to react".

But actually, the root cause is that you care too much about "how others will see me", and then you've made up a whole drama in your head.

The illusion of the "protagonist halo": you always feel like others are staring at you, watching to see if you're making a fool of yourself or saying something wrong.

The truth is: everyone is quite busy, and they really don't have that much time to pay attention to you.

If you don't believe it, think about it: do you remember what the stranger you passed on the road yesterday was wearing?

Others' attention to you is far less than you imagine.

The "disaster movie" we make up: our brains love to scare us.

For example: "What if I go over to say hello and they ignore me? That would be so embarrassing! I'm such a social failure!"

These are all scary scenarios our brains make up to protect us from "making mistakes".

The solution is quite simple: use a few real, peaceful experiences to burst these bubbles we've made up ourselves.

Action one: Try it out, verify that "no one cares".

In places with little pressure, like the supermarket, picking up packages, or waiting at a red light, try saying something very ordinary.

When checking out: "There are quite a few people today."

When picking up packages: "So many packages, thanks for your hard work."

After saying it, see how the other person reacts.

You'll find that the other person either smiles or casually responds.

The sky didn't fall, and no one thought you were strange.

Action two: Use logic to expose the "disaster script".

The next time you feel panicked, you can write it down on your phone.

On the left: Write the worst outcome you're worried about.

For example: "If I stumble during my speech, everyone will laugh at me forever."

On the right: Use common sense to refute it.

For example: "Last week a colleague also stumbled during the meeting, everyone just paused for two seconds, then continued the discussion.

Who remembers?"

Doing this can pull your attention from "I'm so nervous" back to "actually things aren't that scary".

Action three: Protect your battery, set a "stop-loss line".

Don't go head-to-head with socializing.

Clearly know where your "tiredness point" is.

Once you feel your energy can't keep up, immediately activate "power-saving mode".

Take a break: Go to the bathroom for a few minutes, or excuse yourself to take a call.

Listen only, don't speak: Stop actively looking for topics, switch to "yeah, oh, right" listening mode.

Plan your exit time in advance: Before going to a gathering, decide to stay for an hour and then leave.

Having a plan in mind means you won't be anxious about "wanting to leave but feeling bad about it".
textTranslate:
咱们说的"社恐"，很多时候其实是脑子里在"自己吓自己"。

你以为是自个儿"嘴笨"、"反应慢"，其实根儿上，是你太在意"别人会怎么看我"了，然后自己脑补了一出大戏。

错觉的"主角光环"：总觉得别人都在盯着自己，看自己是不是出丑了、说错话了。

其实真相是：大家都挺忙的，真没那么多工夫关注你。

不信你想想，你还记得昨天路上擦肩而过的陌生人穿了啥吗？

别人对你的注意，远没你想象的那么多。

脑补的"灾难大片"：脑子特爱吓唬你。

比如："我要是过去打招呼，他没理我咋办？那也太丢人了！我真是个社交失败者！"

这些都是大脑为了保护你"不出错"而编出来的吓人剧情。

解决办法挺简单：用几次真实、平和的经历，去戳破这些自己脑补出来的泡泡。

行动一：试试看，验证"没人在意"。

在没啥压力的地方（比如超市、取快递、等红灯）试着说句特别平常的话。

结账时："今天人不少哈。"

取快递："快递真多，辛苦了。"

说完看看对方啥反应。

你会发现，对方要么笑笑，要么随口回一句。

天没塌下来，也没人觉得你奇怪。

行动二：用道理，拆穿"灾难剧本"。

下次又觉得心慌时，可以拿手机记一下。

左边：写你担心的最坏结果（比如：发言卡壳了，大家会笑话我一辈子）。

右边：用常理来反驳（比如：上周开会同事也卡壳了，大家也就愣了两秒，接着讨论，谁还记得？）。

这么做，能把你的注意力从"我好紧张"拉回到"其实事情没那么可怕"上来。

行动三：保护电量，设个"止损线"。

咱们别跟社交硬碰硬。

明确知道自己的"累"点在哪里。

一旦觉得精力跟不上了，马上启动"省电模式"。

躲一会儿：去洗手间待几分钟，或者借口接个电话。

只听不说：别再主动找话题，切换到"嗯，哦，是"的倾听模式。

提前想好撤退时间：去聚会前就想好，待够一小时就走。

心里有底，就不会因为"想走又不好意思"而焦虑了。

title: Starting Conversations: Observe First
text:
First, observe with your eyes and ears.

This is your lifeline!

Don't think, just look, listen, and feel.

Scene examples:

At a convenience store queue: What the person in front bought, what the clerk is restocking, today's weather, the music playing in the store.

In an elevator: How many people, what floor we're on, who pressed which floor, the ads in the elevator.

In the office: A colleague's new cup or snacks on their desk, the water dispenser is out of water, the air conditioning temperature, sounds outside the window.

At a relative's house: Fruit or snacks on the coffee table, the program on TV, flowers on the balcony.

Waiting at a restaurant: How many people in line, the menu at the door, what the next table ordered.

Based on what you observe, ask a small question or make a small comment.

The key: Based on your observation, ask a very specific question that the other person can answer in one or two sentences, or make a brief comment that doesn't require a response.

Never ask: "How have you been?" or "Is work busy?"

These questions are too big, the other person will get tired answering, and you won't be able to follow up, which easily leads to awkwardness.

Demonstrations:

At a convenience store queue:

Observation: The person in front bought several cans of coffee.

Small question: "Is the coffee on sale today?"

Small comment: "That coffee looks really energizing."

In an elevator:

Observation: The elevator stopped on a certain floor for a long time.

Small question: "Did someone press this floor?"

Small comment: "The elevator is a bit slow today."

In the office:

Observation: A colleague has a huge thermos on their desk.

Small question: "Your cup is really big, how much water can it hold?"

Small comment: "That cup looks like it could last all day."

If you want to keep the conversation going, gently pass the conversation back.

If you asked a question and the other person answered, and you want to keep the conversation from breaking, but don't want to find a new topic yourself, immediately after the other person answers, briefly respond and gently pass the conversation back.

The core: Keep it brief!

Don't expand!

Examples:

At the convenience store: The clerk says "Coffee is buy one get one half off", you respond: "Oh, I see."

Then you can end it, or ask again: "Which flavor sells the most?" Another specific small question.

In the elevator: Someone says "Yeah, it got stuck", you respond: "Oh, I see."

In the office: The colleague says "Yeah, 1.5 liters", you respond: "That's a lot, impressive."

Small tips:

Your "yeah/oh/I see" plus a nod or smile is completely enough!

This is the most effortless and safe response.

Don't rack your brain for clever words.

It's normal if the conversation doesn't go anywhere!

Use the formula to start, and if the other person also doesn't have much interest in chatting, then naturally be quiet for a moment, look at your phone, or find a reason to leave.

Silence doesn't equal awkwardness.

Forcing conversation is what's awkward.
textTranslate:
先观察（用眼睛看，用耳朵听）。

这是你的救命稻草！

不用想，看、听、感受就行。

场景举例：

便利店排队：前面的人买了啥、店员在补什么货、今天天气、店里放的音乐。

电梯里：人多不多、到几楼了、谁按了哪层、电梯里的广告。

办公室：同事桌上的新杯子或零食、饮水机没水了、空调温度、窗外的声音。

亲戚家：茶几上的水果或零食、电视里放的节目、阳台上的花。

饭馆等位：排队的人多不多、门口的菜单、旁边桌点的菜。

针对观察到的事，问个小问题或发个小感叹。

重点：基于你的观察，问一个特别具体、对方一两句就能答完的问题，或者发出一个简短的小感叹（不需要对方回答那种）。

千万别问："最近怎么样？""工作忙吗？"

这种问题太大，对方答着累，你也接不上，容易尬住。

示范：

便利店排队：

观察：前面大叔买了好几罐咖啡。

小问题："这咖啡今天是特价吗？"

小感叹："这咖啡看着挺提神。"

电梯里：

观察：电梯在某一层停了好久。

小问题："是这层有人按了吗？"

小感叹："今天电梯有点慢哈。"

办公室：

观察：同事桌上有个超大保温杯。

小问题："你这杯子真大，能装多少水啊？"

小感叹："这杯子看着能喝一天。"

如果还想聊，就再把话递回去一点。

如果你问了个问题，对方回答了，你还想让话别断，但自己又不想找新话题，就在对方答完后，立刻、简短地接一句，把话头再轻轻递回去。

核心：简短！别展开！

示范：

便利店：店员说"咖啡第二件半价"，你接："哦，这样啊。"

然后可以结束，或者再问："哪种口味买的人多呀？"又一个具体小问题。

电梯：有人说"是啊，卡了一下"，你接："哦哦，我说呢。"

办公室：同事说"是啊，1.5升的"，你接："真能喝，厉害。"

小提示：

你"嗯、哦、这样啊"加点头或微笑就完全够了！

这是最省力又安全的回应。

不用绞尽脑汁想漂亮话。

聊不下去很正常！

用公式开个头，如果对方也没啥聊的兴致，那就自然地安静一下，看看手机，或者找个理由走开。

安静不等于尴尬，硬找话聊才尴尬。

title: Simple Responses: Being a Good Listener
text:
The core idea: Start by giving simple responses.

You don't need to pursue every response being brilliant.

In most daily conversations, being able to catch what the other person says and let the dialogue flow naturally is already doing very well.

We can first try to become a "friendly responder".

Common scenarios and response ideas:

Scenario: A colleague or friend casually shares a small thing or expresses a feeling.

The other person says: "Ugh, the subway was really crowded this morning, I almost missed it."

Simple responses:

"Rush hour really is crowded." This shows understanding.

"That's really annoying." This expresses empathy.

"Good thing you made it in the end." This views the result positively.

Slightly extended:

"Yeah, especially the transfer section is really crowded." This resonates and makes it specific.

"I had that happen last week too, got really squeezed." This shares a similar experience.

Scenario: The other person states a neutral fact or state.

The other person says: "This coffee tastes okay." or "The project is finally wrapped up."

Simple responses:

"Yeah, it's not bad." or "Congratulations, you can relax a bit now."

Ask a small question if you want to continue the topic:

"What flavor did you get?" For the coffee.

"Can you take it easy for a few days now?" For the completed project.

Scenario: The other person expresses an opinion or evaluation.

The other person says: "I think that new movie was pretty good." or "This newly opened restaurant feels average."

You can respond like this:

"Oh? What did you think was good or average?" This expresses curiosity and encourages the other person to say more.

"I see, I haven't seen it or been there yet." This honestly states your situation.

"Hearing you say that, I'm a bit curious or hesitant." This expresses that their sharing has affected you.

Scenario: Brief interaction with strangers or service staff.

The other person, a delivery person, says: "Your package is a bit heavy."

You can respond:

"Yeah, thanks for your hard work." This expresses thanks and agreement.

"Yeah, thanks." This is a simple acknowledgment.

A sincere smile plus "thank you" is usually enough.

Some simple and practical response phrases:

Expressing agreement: "That's true." or "Yeah, I think so too."

Expressing curiosity: "Oh? Really?" or "What happened next?"

Expressing empathy: "That's not easy." or "That's really hard."

Expressing happiness: "That's great!" or "Congratulations!"

Expressing understanding: "I understand." or "I feel the same way."
textTranslate:
核心思路：从给予简单的回应开始。

不必追求每次回应都精彩绝伦。

在大多数日常交流中，能接住对方的话，让对话自然流动，就已经做得很好。

我们可以先试着成为一个"友好的回应者"。

常见场景与回应思路：

场景：同事或朋友随口分享一件小事或表达感受。

对方说："唉，早上地铁特别挤，差点迟到。"

简单回应：

"早高峰人是真的多。"表示理解。

"那太折腾了。"表达共情。

"还好最后赶上了。"积极看待结果。

稍作延伸：

"是啊，尤其换乘那一段特别挤。"共鸣并具体化。

"我上周也遇到过，被挤得够呛。"分享类似经历。

场景：对方陈述一个中性的事实或状态。

对方说："这咖啡味道还可以。""项目总算告一段落了。"

简单回应：

"嗯，是还不错。""恭喜啊，可以稍微放松一下了。"

提出一个小问题（如果想延续话题）：

"你点的是哪种口味？"针对咖啡。

"接下来能轻松几天了吧？"针对项目完成。

场景：对方表达一个观点或评价。

对方说："我觉得那部新电影挺好看的。""这家新开的餐馆感觉一般。"

可以这样回应：

"哦？你觉得哪里比较好看或一般？"表达好奇，鼓励对方多说。

"这样啊，我还没看过或去过呢。"如实说明自己的情况。

"听你这么说，我有点好奇或有点犹豫了。"表达对方的分享对你产生了影响。

场景：与陌生人或服务人员有简短交流。

对方（快递员）说："您这个件有点分量。"

可以回应：

"是啊，辛苦您了。"表示感谢和认同。

"嗯嗯，麻烦了。"简单附和。

一个真诚的微笑加上"谢谢"，通常就足够了。

一些简单实用的回应句式：

表示认同："确实是这样。""是啊，我也觉得。"

表达好奇："哦？是吗？""后来呢？"

表达共情："不容易。""挺辛苦的。"

表达高兴："太好了！""恭喜啊！"

表达理解："我明白。""有同感。"

title: Low-Effort Responses: Short, Neutral, Easy to Remember
titleTranslate: 省力回应：简短、中性、容易记住
text:
The principle: Short, neutral, easy to remember, no pressure.

Scenario: Meeting neighbors or acquaintances in the elevator or neighborhood.

Starting the conversation: "Going out?" or "Back already?" or "Nice weather today or it's a bit hot."

Talking about the weather is usually safe.

Responding to others: "Yeah, what about you?" or "Yeah, just got back."

Ending the conversation: "I'll head out then." or "Bye!" With a smile and nod.

Scenario: Arriving at the office in the morning.

Greeting: "Morning!" If you remember, you can add the person's name: "Morning, Wang!"

Responding to others: "Morning!" or "Yeah, just got here."

Scenario: Lunch break or meeting colleagues in the break room for casual chat.

Non-work topics.

Showing you're listening: "Oh, I see." or "Really?" or "That's true."

Simple agreement when everyone's mood is consistent: "Haha, exactly." or "You said it."

Don't want to go deeper or want to leave: "I'm going to get some water." or "You guys chat, I need to reply to a message." Then naturally walk away.

Scenario: Checking out at a convenience store or supermarket.

Responding to clerk's greeting: "Hello."

Responding to small talk: "Yeah, it's okay." or "Yeah."

Ending: "Thanks." or "That's all, thanks." Take your things and leave.

Scenario: Ordering or paying at a restaurant.

Ordering: "Hello, I'll have set A or XX noodles." or "Can I order, please?"

Responding to confirmation: "Yeah, that's all." or "Add one more XX, thanks."

Calling for service: "Hello, can I get some water or check out, please?"

Leaving: "Thanks." or "Check, please."

Scenario: Answering delivery or package phone calls.

Confirming: "Hello, just leave it at the door or front desk, thanks!"

If you need them to wait: "Just a moment, I'll be right down or open the door."

Receiving the item: "Thanks, you've worked hard!"

Scenario: Wanting to politely decline an invitation you don't really want to attend.

Concise version: "Thanks for the invitation! I'm not available this time, have fun!"

Version with reason: "Thanks! I have something at home today or I'm a bit tired and want to rest, maybe next time!"

"Next time" is a polite expression, don't feel pressured.

Key points: Thank for the invitation, clearly decline, brief reason if needed, wish them well.

No need for excessive explanation.

Scenario: Asking someone to help with a small favor, like passing something.

"Could you help me pass that, please? Thanks!" or "Can you help me pick that up? Thanks!"

Scenario: Saying goodbye when leaving work.

"I'm heading out!" or "See you tomorrow!" or "Bye!" To colleagues who are still there.

Responding to others' goodbyes: "Bye!" or "See you tomorrow!" or "Take care on the way home."
textTranslate:
原则：简短、中性、容易记住、没有压力。

场景：在电梯或小区遇到邻居或半熟人。

开启对话："出去啊？"或"回来啦？"或"今天天气不错或有点热"。

聊天气通常很安全。

回应对方："是啊，你呢？"或"嗯嗯，刚回来。"

结束对话："那我先走了啊。"或"拜拜！"配合微笑点头。

场景：早上到办公室。

打招呼："早！"如果记得，可以加上对方称呼："早，王哥！"

回应他人："早！"或"嗯，刚到。"

场景：午休或茶水间遇到同事闲聊（非工作话题）。

表示在听："哦，这样啊。"或"是嘛？"或"确实。"

简单附和（当大家情绪一致时）："哈哈，就是。"或"可不是嘛。"

不想深入或想离开："我先去接点水。"或"你们聊，我回个信息。"然后自然走开。

场景：在便利店或超市结账。

回应店员问候："你好。"

回应闲聊："是啊或还行。"或"嗯嗯。"

结束："谢谢。"或"好了，谢谢。"拿好东西离开。

场景：在餐厅点餐或结账。

点餐："你好，要一份A套餐或XX面。"或"麻烦点单。"

回应确认："嗯，就这些。"或"再加一杯XX，谢谢。"

呼叫服务："你好，麻烦加杯水或结账。"

离开："谢谢。"或"买单。"

场景：接外卖或快递电话。

确认："喂你好，放门口或前台就行，谢谢！"

如需对方稍等："稍等一下，我马上下来或开门。"

接到物品："谢谢，辛苦了！"

场景：想婉拒一个不太想去的邀约。

简洁版："谢谢邀请！这次不太方便，你们玩得开心！"

带理由版："谢谢！今天家里有点事或有点累想休息，下次有机会再约！"

"下次"是客气的说法，不用感到压力。

要点：感谢邀请，明确婉拒，简短理由（可选），祝福对方。

无需过多解释。

场景：请人帮个小忙（如递东西）。

"麻烦帮我递一下那个好吗？谢谢！"或"能帮我捡一下吗？谢谢啦！"

场景：下班时道别。

"我先走了啊！"或"明天见！"或"拜拜！"对还在的同事说。

回应他人道别："拜拜！"或"明天见！"或"路上慢点。"

title: Expressing Gratitude at Gatherings
titleTranslate: 在聚会场合如何表达心意
text:
At some gatherings, we sometimes want to raise a glass to elders, leaders, friends, or colleagues to express our feelings.

This can make many people who aren't used to being the center of attention feel a bit pressured.

Actually, expressing feelings doesn't require flowery words.

Sincerity, simplicity, and clarity are enough.

Some ideas we can refer to:

When you need to raise a glass to someone, you can try this simple structure: Address the person, say one sincere and genuine sentence, then raise your glass.

Address the person: Clearly say the person's title, like "Manager Zhang", "Aunt Wang", "Old Li".

This makes it clear who you're addressing.

One genuine sentence: This sentence is the core.

It can be a word of thanks, like "Thank you for your usual guidance", or "Thanks everyone for your hard work today".

It can also be a blessing, like "Wish you good health", or "Wish the project success".

Choose the one that best fits your relationship and the situation.

If you can combine thanks and blessings, like "Thank you for your help, wish you all the best", that's also good.

Raise your glass: After speaking, naturally raise your glass to the person, and you can say "A toast to you" or "Let's drink together".

What you can say in different situations:

At a company gathering:

To a leader: "Manager Zhang, thank you for your guidance during this time, this toast is for you, wish the project success!"

To a colleague: "Brother Liu, thanks for working together, a toast to you, hope we can continue learning from each other!"

At a friend gathering:

To the organizer: "Old Zhang, thanks for organizing again, I must toast you!"

To a friend: "Long time no see, a toast to you, wish you all the best!"

At a family gathering:

To an elder: "Grandpa, wish you good health and long life, a toast to you!"

To parents: "Dad, Mom, you've worked hard, wish you happiness every day, a toast to you!"

Some small tips to note:

Keep it brief: Once the sentiment is expressed, that's enough.

No need for long speeches.

A few simple sentences, then everyone raises their glasses and drinks together, and the atmosphere is harmonious.

Moderate volume: Make sure the other person can hear you, but no need to deliberately raise your voice.

Sincere attitude: The most important thing is your sentiment.

A sincere smile is more important than any beautiful words.

Do what you can: If you can't handle alcohol, it's completely fine to use tea, drinks, or water instead, and say so openly.

For example: "I'll use tea instead of wine, a toast to you, the sentiment is definitely there!"

Expressing feelings at gatherings is a way to convey friendliness and respect.

We don't need to pursue being the center of attention.

We just need to use a way that feels comfortable to us, sincerely express that gratitude or blessing, and that's enough.
textTranslate:
在一些聚会场合，有时我们会想向长辈、领导、朋友或同事举杯，表达一下心意。

这可能让很多不习惯成为焦点的人感到有点压力。

其实，表达心意不一定需要华丽的辞藻，真诚、简洁、清晰就很好。

我们可以参考的一些思路：

当你需要向他人举杯时，可以试试这个简单的结构：称呼对方，说一句真诚的实在话，举杯示意。

称呼对方：清晰地说出对方的称呼，比如"张经理"、"王阿姨"、"老李"。

这能明确你在对谁表达。

一句实在话：这句话是核心。

它可以是一句感谢，比如"感谢您平时的指导"，或者"谢谢大家今天的辛苦"。

也可以是一句祝福，比如"祝您身体健康"、"祝项目顺利"。

选择最贴合你们关系和当时情境的一句就好。

如果能把感谢和祝福结合起来，比如"感谢您的帮助，祝您一切顺利"，也很好。

举杯示意：说完后，自然地向对方举杯，并可以说"敬您一杯"或"和大家一起喝一杯"。

在不同场合可以怎么说：

在公司聚会：

对领导："张经理，感谢您这段时间的指导，这杯敬您，祝项目顺利！"

对同事："刘哥，平时合作辛苦了，敬你一杯，希望以后继续互相学习！"

在朋友聚会：

对组织者："老张，又辛苦你组局了，必须敬你一杯！"

对朋友："好久不见，敬你一杯，祝你一切都好！"

在家庭聚会：

对长辈："爷爷，祝您身体健康，福如东海，敬您！"

对父母："爸、妈，你们辛苦了，祝你们天天开心，敬你们！"

一些可以留意的小提示：

简短为宜：心意到了即可，不需要长篇大论。

简单几句说完，大家举杯同饮，气氛就很融洽。

音量适中：确保对方能听清，但不必刻意提高音量。

态度真诚：最重要的是你的心意。

一个真诚的微笑，比任何漂亮话都重要。

量力而行：如果不胜酒力，完全可以用茶、饮料或水来代替，并大方说明。

比如："我以茶代酒，敬您一杯，心意绝对到！"

在聚会中表达心意，是传递友好和尊重的一种方式。

我们不必追求成为全场的焦点，只需用自己感到舒适的方式，真诚地表达那份感谢或祝福，就足够了。

title: Gift Selection Guide: Consider the Person, Occasion, and Budget
titleTranslate: 礼物挑选指南：看人、看场合、看预算
text:
When selecting gifts, we can consider three aspects: the person, the occasion, and the budget.

For classmates, colleagues, and other ordinary friends:

These situations might include the end of group work, a colleague's probation period completion, team celebrations, etc.

There are some practical and appropriate options.

Gift cards let the other person choose freely, which is one of the most worry-free methods.

A fresh and light-scented scented candle, a small potted plant, or a box of quality snacks are all practical and decent choices.

For teachers, mentors, or leaders:

These gifts are used to express thanks or respect, and the occasions may be relatively formal.

For a team or group:

When you want to reward or thank the entire team, the choice needs to consider everyone.

Distributing to a group has its techniques:

If it's a gift for multiple people, you can place it in a common area and let everyone know, or quickly walk around and distribute it with a brief explanation.

For example: "I brought some snacks for everyone, help yourselves!" or "There's fruit in the break room, everyone can have some."

The key is to be natural and not make a big deal out of it.

When giving gifts, remember:

The most important thing is the sentiment, not the price.

A thoughtful gift that suits the person and occasion is better than an expensive but inappropriate one.

If you're not sure what to give, a gift card or a quality snack box are safe choices.

When in doubt, choose something practical and useful.

Most people appreciate gifts that they can actually use.

Don't feel pressured to spend beyond your budget.

A sincere gift within your means is perfectly fine.

If you're close to the person, you can ask them what they need or like.

This avoids giving something they don't want or can't use.

After giving a gift, you don't need to keep emphasizing it.

A simple "Hope you like it" is enough.

Don't make the other person feel obligated to use it immediately or praise it excessively.
textTranslate:
挑选礼物时，我们可以从三个方面考虑：看人、看场合、看预算。

送给同学、同事等关系普通的朋友：

这类场景可能包括小组合作结束、同事转正、团队庆祝等。

有一些实用又体面的选择。

礼品卡让对方自由选择，是最省心的方法之一。

一份味道清新淡雅的香薰蜡烛、一盆小绿植、一盒品质不错的零食，都是实用又体面的选择。

送给老师、导师或领导：

这类礼物用于表达感谢或敬意，场合可能相对正式。

送给团队或小组集体：

当想要犒劳或感谢整个团队时，选择需要兼顾大家。

集体分发有技巧：

如果是给多人的礼物，可以放在公共区域并告诉大家，或者快速走一圈分发并简单说明。

比如："我带了点零食给大家，随便吃！"或"茶水间有水果，大家自取。"

关键是自然，不用太刻意。

送礼物时记住：

最重要的是心意，不是价格。

一个适合对方和场合的贴心礼物，比昂贵但不合适的礼物更好。

如果不知道送什么，礼品卡或一盒品质不错的零食是安全的选择。

不确定时，选择实用、有用的东西。

大多数人都会喜欢能实际使用的礼物。

不要感到压力去超出预算。

在能力范围内的真诚礼物就很好。

如果和对方关系比较近，可以问问他们需要什么或喜欢什么。

这样可以避免送他们不想要或用不上的东西。

送完礼物后，不需要一直强调。

简单说一句"希望你喜欢"就够了。

不要让对方感到必须立即使用或过度赞美。

title: New Employee: How to Quickly Establish Yourself
titleTranslate: 新人入职：如何快速站稳脚跟
text:
Starting a new job can feel overwhelming.

You're in a new environment, meeting new colleagues, learning new systems, and trying to figure out how things work.

For introverted people, this can be especially challenging.

But don't worry, you don't need to become best friends with everyone immediately.

We can try some simple and natural methods to gradually let everyone get to know you, and help you get familiar with things too.

Start with small interactions:

You don't need to make a big impression.

Start with some daily small details that can convey your friendliness.

In the morning, when you arrive at your desk, you can nod and say "Morning" to the colleague next to you.

This is a basic operation to maintain a friendly atmosphere.

When you see someone carrying something heavy, you can offer: "Need help?"

If they say no, that's fine.

If they say yes, you've made a small positive interaction.

Find your own rhythm in communication:

Participating in conversations doesn't necessarily mean being witty and eloquent.

Finding a way that makes you feel comfortable can also work very well.

You don't need to force yourself to join every conversation.

When others are chatting, you can listen and nod occasionally.

If you have something to say, say it.

If not, that's fine too.

Being a good listener is also a form of participation.

Some common scenario responses:

When someone asks about your previous job:

You can briefly say: "I worked at XX company before, mainly doing XX work."

No need to go into too much detail unless they ask.

When someone offers to help:

Accept it gratefully: "Thank you so much, that's really helpful!"

When you need to ask for help:

Be direct and clear: "Sorry to bother you, could you help me with XX? I'm not familiar with this yet."

When you make a small mistake:

Don't over-apologize.

Simply say: "Sorry about that, I'll be more careful next time."

Then fix it and move on.

Remember:

You don't need to be perfect.

Everyone makes mistakes, especially when they're new.

It's okay to ask questions.

It's better to ask than to guess and make mistakes.

Take your time.

You don't need to figure everything out in the first week.

Give yourself time to adjust and learn.

Be patient with yourself.

Starting a new job is a process.

It's normal to feel a bit lost at first.

You'll gradually find your place and feel more comfortable.
textTranslate:
开始一份新工作可能会让人感到不知所措。

你在一个新环境里，遇到新同事，学习新系统，试图弄清楚事情是如何运作的。

对于内向的人来说，这可能尤其具有挑战性。

但别担心，你不需要立即和每个人都成为最好的朋友。

我们可以试试用一些简单自然的方法，慢慢让大家认识你，也帮你自己熟悉起来。

从微小的互动开始：

不需要刻意表现。

从一些日常的小细节入手，就能传递你的友好。

早上，当你到达工位时，你可以向旁边的同事点头说"早"。

这是维持友好氛围的基本操作。

当你看到有人拿着重物时，你可以主动说："需要帮忙吗？"

如果他们说不用，那也没关系。

如果他们说需要，你就完成了一次小的积极互动。

在交流中找到自己的节奏：

参与对话不一定非要妙语连珠。

找到让你感到舒适的方式，同样能很好地参与。

你不需要强迫自己加入每一次对话。

当别人在聊天时，你可以倾听并偶尔点头。

如果你有话要说，就说。

如果没有，也没关系。

做一个好的倾听者也是一种参与方式。

一些常见场景的应对思路：

当有人问起你之前的工作时：

你可以简短地说："我之前在XX公司工作，主要做XX工作。"

除非他们问，否则不需要说太多细节。

当有人主动提供帮助时：

感激地接受："非常感谢，这真的很有帮助！"

当你需要寻求帮助时：

直接而清晰："不好意思打扰一下，能帮我看看XX吗？我对这个还不熟悉。"

当你犯了一个小错误时：

不要过度道歉。

简单地说："抱歉，我下次会更小心的。"

然后改正它，继续前进。

记住：

你不需要完美。

每个人都会犯错，尤其是当他们还是新人的时候。

问问题是可以的。

问问题总比猜测和犯错要好。

慢慢来。

你不需要在第一周就弄清楚所有事情。

给自己时间调整和学习。

对自己要有耐心。

开始一份新工作是一个过程。

一开始感到有点迷茫是正常的。

你会逐渐找到自己的位置，感到更舒适。

title: Asking Colleagues for Help: What to Pay Attention To
titleTranslate: 请同事帮忙：要注意什么
text:
At work, we often need our colleagues' cooperation and help.

This isn't "asking for favors", it's normal teamwork.

How can we clearly make a request and make it easier for the other person to help?

Before making a request, adjust your mindset:

Cooperation is mutual.

Today you ask someone to check data, tomorrow someone might ask you about PPT skills.

Healthy workplace relationships are built on mutual support.

Don't think of asking for help as a burden.

It's a normal part of work.

How to clearly make a request:

A clear request usually includes several elements: background, specific need, time frame, and your own efforts.

Background: Briefly explain why you need help.

For example: "I'm working on the monthly report, but I'm not familiar with the data system yet."

Specific need: Clearly state what you need.

For example: "Could you help me pull the sales data for last month?"

Time frame: Let them know when you need it.

For example: "I need it by this afternoon if possible."

Your own efforts: Show that you've tried.

For example: "I've looked through the manual, but I'm still not sure how to do it."

If the other person can't help:

If the other person says they can't assist, you can respond like this:

"No problem, thanks anyway!"

"I understand, I'll try another way."

"Thanks for letting me know, I'll ask someone else."

Don't take it personally.

They might really be busy or not have the information you need.

After getting help:

Always say thank you.

"Thanks so much, that really helped!"

If appropriate, you can offer to help them in return.

"If you ever need help with anything, just let me know!"

Remember:

Be clear and direct.

Vague requests are harder to fulfill.

Be respectful of their time.

If it's urgent, say so.

If it can wait, let them know.

Show appreciation.

A simple thank you goes a long way.

Don't overthink it.

Asking for help is normal.

Everyone needs help sometimes.

It's part of being a team.
textTranslate:
在工作中，我们时常需要同事的配合与帮助。

这并非"求人"，而是正常的团队协作。

如何清晰地提出请求，让对方更容易帮助你呢？

提出请求前，先调整好心态：

协作是相互的。

今天你请别人核对数据，明天别人可能问你PPT技巧。

健康的职场关系本就建立在相互支持的基础上。

不要把请求帮助当作负担。

这是工作的正常部分。

如何清晰地提出请求：

一个清晰的请求通常包含几个要素：事情背景、具体需求、时间节点，以及你已经做的努力。

背景：简要说明为什么需要帮助。

例如："我正在做月度报告，但我对数据系统还不熟悉。"

具体需求：清楚地说明你需要什么。

例如："能帮我拉一下上个月的销售数据吗？"

时间节点：让他们知道你需要的时间。

例如："如果可能的话，今天下午之前需要。"

你的努力：表明你已经尝试过。

例如："我已经看过手册了，但还是不确定怎么做。"

如果对方不方便帮忙：

如果对方表示无法协助，可以这样应对：

"没问题，还是谢谢你！"

"我理解，我会试试其他方法。"

"谢谢告知，我会问问其他人。"

不要往心里去。

他们可能真的很忙，或者没有你需要的信息。

得到帮助后：

一定要说谢谢。
